paper.title: An Asymptotically Optimal Policy for Finite Support Models in the Multiarmed Bandit Problem

settings.name_in_paper: K-armed bandit with finite bounded support model A
unmapped: Reward distributions have finite support contained in a known interval [a,b] (wlog [-1,0]); the specific support is unknown
settings.definition_quote: Let $\fb\equiv\{F:|\supp(F)|<\infty,\,\supp(F)\subset [a,b]\}$ be the family of distributions with a {\em finite} bounded support, where $\supp(F)$ is the support of distribution $F$ and $a,b$ are constants known to the player.

symbols.c_0: O(1) term, constant in N (depends on the instance and eps)

conditions: all arm distributions have finite support in the known interval [-1,0] (wlog [a,b])

source.label: optMD
source.quote: Fix $\bm{F}\in\fb^K$ satisfying $\mu_j=\mu^*$ and $\mu_i<\mu^*$ for all $i\neq j$. Under MED policy, for any $i\neq j$ and $\ep>0$ it holds that \E_{\bm{F}}[T_i(N)]\le \frac{1+\ep}{\dmin(F_i,\mu^*,\fb)}\log N +\lo(1).

results.notes: Bound on the expected pull count of a suboptimal arm i (quantity 'other'); multiplying by Delta_i and summing gives pseudo-regret. D_min(F_i,mu*,A) = D_inf (Lemma 2), i.e. Kinf_i for the finite-support model. The paper derives limsup E[T_i(N)]/log N <= 1/D_min, which shows asymptotic optimality. Corollary 1 states the same bound with D_min over A_X for any support set X containing 0; it is weaker and follows from this theorem.

cited_results.cited_title: Optimal adaptive policies for sequential allocation problems
cited_results.setting_description: Stochastic K-armed bandit with a general (nonparametric) model F; consistent policies; expected number of pulls of a suboptimal arm i with 0 < D_inf < infinity
